quizzes.title: Advantages of Polymer Notes (MCQ)
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India has revived a proposal to introduce polymer-based banknotes in India. Polymer currency notes are manufactured using a specialised plastic substrate, primarily Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene, instead of conventional cotton-based banknote paper. The idea is not new, as an initial proposal was made in 2009. Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI, has invited global bids for a BOPP-based polymer substrate to manufacture polymer banknotes. Banknotes in India are printed at four currency printing presses, and together they print all the banknotes of India in different denominations. Under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the RBI issues banknotes, estimates the country's currency requirements and maintains an adequate supply of banknotes. The Government of India, on the other hand, approves the design and material of banknotes based on recommendations of the RBI's Central Board. Coins are minted under the Coinage Act, 2011, and are then supplied to the RBI, which distributes them to banks and the public. The RBI has also introduced a Clean Note Policy so that the public receives currency notes and coins of acceptable quality. Currency, coinage, legal tender and foreign exchange fall within the legislative domain of the Union Government under the Union List.

questions.q: Polymer banknotes are described as more resistant to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists polymer banknotes as more resistant to tearing.

questions.q: Polymer substrates allow the integration of which kind of feature that is much harder for counterfeiters to replicate?
questions.explanation: The booklet says polymer substrates allow sophisticated security features that are much harder to replicate compared to paper.

questions.q: Because individual polymer notes last longer, what happens to the number of new notes that must be made?
options: More new notes must be printed each year
New notes must be imported from abroad
Fewer new notes need to be manufactured and issued
Printing presses must be shut down
questions.explanation: The booklet says fewer new notes need to be manufactured and issued to maintain a steady supply.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Polymer banknotes need less frequent replacement cycles.
Reason (R): Polymer banknotes remain usable for significantly longer periods.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The booklet links the longer usable life of polymer notes to less frequent replacement cycles, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Sophisticated features integrated into the substrate   ->   A. Less vulnerable to water and moisture
II. Longer usable life of each note   ->   B. Fewer new notes need to be manufactured
III. Exposure to humidity   ->   C. Much harder to replicate than on paper
IV. Stress of being pulled apart   ->   D. More resistant to tearing
questions.explanation: Sophisticated features match C, longer life matches B, humidity matches A, and being pulled apart matches D.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about polymer banknotes:
I. They are more resistant to tearing.
II. They are made from cotton-based banknote paper.
III. They remain usable for significantly longer periods.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because polymer notes are made from a plastic substrate instead of cotton-based paper.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about polymer banknotes:
Statement 1: They are less vulnerable to water and moisture.
Statement 2: They are made from cotton-based banknote paper.
Statement 3: They can incorporate advanced anti-counterfeiting features.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, while statement 2 is wrong because polymer notes replace cotton-based paper.

questions.explanation: The booklet lists polymer banknotes as less vulnerable to water and moisture.

questions.q: Polymer banknotes are more resistant to what kind of action, in one word?
questions.explanation: The booklet says polymer banknotes are more resistant to tearing.

questions.q: Because individual polymer notes last longer, fewer what need to be manufactured to keep supply steady? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says fewer new notes need to be manufactured and issued to keep supply steady.

questions.q: Polymer notes last longer, so replacement cycles are needed less what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the longevity of polymer notes means less frequent replacement cycles.

questions.q: Polymer banknotes are more durable under what kind of usage? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says polymer notes are more durable under frequent circulation.

questions.q: Less frequent replacement of polymer notes lowers which kind of environmental footprint over time? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says less frequent replacement lowers the long-term environmental footprint.

questions.q: Polymer substrates allow the integration of what kind of features? (two words)

quizzes.title: Costs and Challenges of Polymer Notes (MCQ)
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India has revived a proposal to introduce polymer-based banknotes in India, after an initial proposal was made in 2009. Polymer currency notes are made from a substrate instead of the paper used for conventional banknotes. Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI, has invited global bids for a substrate to manufacture polymer banknotes. The Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited will print polymer notes. The Government of India approves the design and material of banknotes based on recommendations of the RBI's Central Board. The RBI issues banknotes, estimates the country's currency requirements and maintains an adequate supply of banknotes. Banknotes in India are printed at four currency printing presses. Coins are minted at four government-owned mints located in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Noida, under the Coinage Act, 2011. Currency, coinage, legal tender and foreign exchange fall within the legislative domain of the Union Government under the Union List. The RBI introduced a Clean Note Policy so that the public receives currency notes and coins of acceptable quality. The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 provides the principal legal framework for issuing banknotes and managing currency. Coins are supplied to the RBI after minting, and the RBI distributes them through its currency management network to banks and the public.

questions.q: The production cost of polymer notes is tied to which global factor?
questions.explanation: The booklet says polymer note production cost is tied to global oil prices.

questions.q: Unlike cotton-based paper, polymer notes raise concerns about which issue?
questions.explanation: The booklet says polymer notes raise serious concerns regarding plastic waste management.

questions.q: The transition to polymer notes requires recalibration of which machines?
options: ATMs, currency vending machines and automated cash-handling machines
questions.explanation: The booklet lists ATMs, currency vending machines and automated cash-handling machines as needing recalibration.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Polymer notes raise concerns about plastic waste.
Reason (R): Plastic waste needs an effective specialised collection and recycling system.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the need for a recycling system does not explain why the concern arises.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Material from which polymer notes are made   ->   A. Polypropylene
II. Foreign sourcing of that material   ->   B. Import dependency
III. Handling plastic waste from notes   ->   C. Specialised collection and recycling system
IV. Effect on banking and retail infrastructure   ->   D. Substantial secondary expenses
questions.explanation: Polymer notes are made from polypropylene, reliance on it creates import dependency, plastic waste needs a specialised system, and the transition brings secondary expenses.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about polymer banknotes:
I. Their production cost is tied to global oil prices.
II. They are made from cotton-based banknote paper.
III. Their transition requires changes to ATMs and vending machines.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while statement II is wrong because polymer notes are made from plastic instead of cotton-based paper.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about polymer banknotes:
Statement 1: Polymer notes cost significantly more to produce than conventional paper currency.
Statement 2: They are made from cotton-based banknote paper.
Statement 3: Their transition requires changes to automated cash-handling machines.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, while statement 2 is wrong.
